body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 29, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a mix of news from overnight. Today’s top story is the tragic crash on Copus Road that left three dead and several injured. We’re also tracking a return to high school football games under new safety measures following last week’s Independence High School shooting. Right now, we’re looking at partly sunny skies and a high near 95 degrees, with an overnight low around 70. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 81. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Kern County saw its share of activity. Around 10:55 p.m., fire crews and a battalion chief were dispatched to a grass fire near the Hampton Inn on East Brundage Lane by the freeway. Meanwhile, shortly after 4 a.m., medical crews responded to a possible overdose outside Brookside on Coffee Road, where a person was found unconscious but breathing. Elsewhere, officers handled a domestic disturbance at an apartment on Lincoln Street just after 11 p.m., and deputies checked on a Grand Prairie Drive home around 11:30 p.m. after the resident reported someone on the roof. The night also included a diabetic emergency on West Mariposa Avenue and a welfare check on a vehicle passenger near Wofford Heights.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for partly sunny skies with a high near 95 degrees. The overnight low is expected to dip to around 70 degrees. Right now, it’s 73 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County at this time, and air quality is moderate with an AQI of 81. 

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that three people are dead and several others are injured following a crash on Copus Road.** The collision occurred late Friday night and involved multiple vehicles. Emergency responders were dispatched to the scene, where they found a chaotic situation with several people trapped in the wreckage. The victims were pronounced dead at the scene, and the injured were transported to local hospitals. The road was closed for several hours as investigators worked to determine the cause of the crash. This tragic incident has left the community in mourning and serves as a stark reminder of the dangers on our roads.

**According to 23ABC, fans returned to the stands for the first varsity football game since the Independence High School shooting.** The Liberty Patriots played on their home field against the Menlo-Atherton Bears, and while the atmosphere was lively, safety was clearly a top priority. New security measures were in place, including increased police presence and additional security at the stadium. Students had their school IDs checked at the entrance, and bags were searched. For some students, the extra precautions helped ease their fears, while others said the added security made them feel more comfortable returning to the games. The crowd turnout was strong, with the stands filled and fans cheering on their teams.

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield College’s robot-powered automation program is celebrating its 10th anniversary.** The program, which started with just seven graduates, has grown to a record class of 34 this year. The industrial automation lab has added a four-legged robotic dog and a new humanoid model to its roster of training tools. The program was launched to address the shortage of skilled workers in Kern County, and it has since become a vital resource for local employers. BC reports a 98% job-placement rate among graduates seeking work, and many students begin working before graduation. Each spring, a career fair draws employers from across the country to recruit prospective graduates.

## Something good

Kern County is celebrating a remarkable milestone today: a local World War II veteran is turning 102 years old. This birthday is a testament to a life well-lived and a cause for celebration in our community. It’s a reminder of the resilience and spirit that define Kern County, and we wish our veteran a very happy birthday.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several events and meetings on the calendar for Kern County residents. On Tuesday, September 2, the Personnel and Processes Committee will meet at 12:00 p.m. Later that day, the Police Civil Service Commission will convene at 8:30 p.m. On Wednesday, September 3, the Planning Commission will hold its meeting at 5:30 p.m. For those looking for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule: tonight, catch Willie Barcena or the Danny ELBC Presents: Michael Return Of The King Tribute. On Thursday, September 4, enjoy the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA or The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies. And on Friday, September 5, Talib Kweli will take the stage for a one-night-only performance in Bakersfield.
